who: claude-fable-5-2 (Claude Fable 5.2), main agent in Claude Code, port of the front end onto blaze-memo; first read out of the code by a Claude Opus 5.5 lane merging main
where: crates/blaze-memo/src: task.rs (`push`, `Pushed::drop`, `innermost`, `Run::new`), attach.rs (`attach`, its restore, `attached`, `shallow`), arena.rs (`with_local`), counts.rs (`bump`, `completed_one`, `take_counts`)
what: Every thread-local read of blaze-memo was in a function the compiler may inline into a fetch, and a fetch spans its run's function, which may park the fiber and resume on another worker. A function that reads a thread-local and waits may keep the thread-local's address from before the wait (crates/blaze-graph/src/sched/fiber.rs says so, and it is the cause of the 2026-11-02 `RefCell already borrowed` in the pool). Here that means: a run popped off the worker it left, a database restored onto it, counts added to its cell, and worst, `with_local` handing the second allocation of a fetch the first worker's bump allocators (`LOCALS`), two threads in one allocator. Not observed failing; found by reading.
cost: none measured; the class is the one behind a segfault of blaze on reth on main, so it was fixed before the port ran on fibers at scale
cause: blaze-memo was written against the rule in its text (the stack of runs and the attached database are carried with the job across waits) but not against the rule in its codegen: carrying moves the value, and an inlined reader still uses the old thread's address.
whys: the rule lives in a module comment of another crate (sched/fiber.rs); the lint that holds it, `thread_local_in_waiting_fn`, does not see a reader two calls down or a wait reached through a type parameter (`Q::run`), which is exactly a memo's fetch; a debug-build test cannot show it (nothing is inlined), so no test of blaze-memo could fail for it
class: a thread-local read that can be inlined into a function that spans a fiber wait
prevention: built: each thread-local read of blaze-memo is behind an `#[inline(never)]` reader that returns the value, never the address (a function returning the address reads no memory, so two calls of it may be merged across the wait all the same). Owed: a strict form of `thread_local_in_waiting_fn` for crates that run on fibers (every `LocalKey` read sits in an `#[inline(never)]` function that makes no call that may park), which closes both blind spots for those crates; and its findings on the front end's own thread-locals (hir-def, hir-ty, base-db have about ninety) now that their queries run on blaze-memo. The end state is the may-suspend design's: codegen recomputes a thread-local's address after a call that may suspend (docs/v2/plan/design/may-suspend.md), and the reader rule goes.
state: fixed in the port checkout, uncommitted at the time of writing (after port snapshot 22c); blaze-memo check-compiles on the Mac; not yet in a round on blaze-vm
